articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He's Done With Franchise Films After Resident Evil
articles.summary: Resident Evil movie director Zach Cregger is days away from his survival horror adaptation's theatrical premiere, but don't expect to help bring another franchise film to the big screen ever again.
body: The filmmaker behind this month's Capcom project talked about what's next for him during a conversation with Deadline. When asked if he's ever been pressured to spearhead another recognizable IP, he gave a blunt answer: "I'm not doing that."

"I have never been approached by another franchise," Cregger said. "Maybe I have, but it would never get to me because I have been very clear that I’m not doing that. I’m doing this, and that’s it for me."

One might suspect Cregger's aversion to big franchise films like Resident Evil might stem from the backlash he's received in the months leading up to his movie's premiere. While the Barbarian and Weapons creator certainly has plenty of defenders looking forward to seeing his new live-action take, there have been many, many others who aren't quite as excited.

Most of the pressure has come from those who feel his Resident Evil doesn't align with the game it's based on. Changes to the source material, including its modern setting and snowy Raccoon City, have set fans on edge, while others aren't in love with the idea of following a new protagonist (Austin Abrams' Bryan Hodukavich) instead of someone like Leon S. Kennedy or Claire Redfield.
points: Resident Evil movie director Zach Cregger is days away from his survival horror adaptation's theatrical premiere, but don't expect to help bring another franchise film to the big screen ever again.

articles.title: Primetime Review
articles.summary: A blast from the past with a sickly allure, the Robert Pattinson romp Primetime is as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.
body: This review is based on a screening from the Venice Film Festival. Primetime is in theaters on September 25.

You don’t have to be familiar with Chris Hansen or To Catch a Predator to enjoy Primetime — director Lance Oppenheim’s feature debut — but it certainly helps. That’s not because the movie sticks closely to real events, but rather, because it takes some audacious swings while purposefully fudging the timeline. Watching exactly how and why it takes these liberties is a delight of its own; the result is a sleazy, rollicking, razor-wire drama that’s every bit about the rise of reality TV as it is a spiritual part of it. Anything is fair game if it makes for a good story.
points: A blast from the past with a sickly allure, the Robert Pattinson romp Primetime is as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.

body: This year marks the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda, and it’s finally time to get the party started. On Tuesday, Sept. 8, Nintendo will host The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. The 30-minute stream promises to “deliver a variety of The Legend of Zelda related information.” That’s a bit of a clinical description, but the vague wording makes sense when you consider what Nintendo could reveal during the stream.

The main event of this showcase is undoubtedly The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo has said next to nothing about its Switch 2 remake since it was first teased, even though it’s supposed to launch sometime in the next few months. Expect a blowout here that gives us a real look at the visuals, a deep dive into gameplay, and a release date. Nintendo might save a few of the finer details for its Treehouse stream the next day, but all the major bullet points should be here.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Passes 1 Million Copies Sold in Just 2 Days
articles.summary: Single-player RPG and new IP The Blood of Dawnwalker has sold 1 million copies just two days after its launch, publisher Bandai Namco and developer Rebel Wolves have announced.
body: Official social media accounts for the first-time developer's new game confirmed the news with a celebratory graphic today. The milestone was reached just 48 hours after The Blood of Dawnwalker launched for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3.
"Thank you for playing, sharing, supporting, and being part of the community!" Rebel Wolves said in a message to fans.

An official summary for The Blood of Dawnwalker describes it as an "open-world dark fantasy action RPG set in 14th-century Europe." In this first chapter, players take the role of Coen, a "human by day and vampire by night" who is fighting for his family in a narrative shaped by player choice. It also happens to have an in-game clock that sees Coen's story take place through a 30-day period. It's something some players love – and others don't.

articles.summary: Season 2 of Guy Ritchie ’s stylish crime drama The Gentlemen was released on Netflix on Sept. 3. It’s easy to binge the eight episodes, which are packed with chase scenes, bloody shootouts, gorgeous sets, and convoluted schemes.
body: Yes! Netflix and Ritchie announced that the show had been renewed in August, about a week before the season 2 premiere.

In The Gentlemen season 1, Eddie returns home from serving as a United Nations peacekeeping officer after his father’s death and learns that a marijuana grow house was operating on his family’s estate. After initially trying to clear his debt to the gang leader Bobby Glass (Ray Winstone), Eddie decides to get deeper into the drug game as a way to restore his estate to its former glory.

That leads to a series of questionable schemes in season 2. Eddie becomes a hereditary peer in the House of Lords in the hopes of passing legislation to decriminalize marijuana, even though Glass wants to kill the bill. He borrows money from Italian mob boss Marco Moretti (Sergio Castellitto) to fund the expansion and winds up having to leverage his estate as collateral to get a loan from the billionaire Fred Johnston (Giancarlo Esposito) to pay Moretti back when the vote fails. Bobby, in turn, buys the debt from Johnston to gain more control over Eddie, who he believes is “evolving” into a worthy inheritor of his drug empire.

articles.title: 7 R-Rated Action Movies That Are 10/10, No Notes
articles.summary: Great action movies also have stakes that feel real. They break genre conventions, use fights to flesh out characters, and balance out frenetic action with quieter moments. With these factors in mind, here are seven R-rated action movies that are 10 out of 10.
body: There’s more to an R-rated action flick than intense violence or brutal fight choreography. Although most R-rated genre films indulge in graphic violence, this rating primarily accommodates a mature story with nuanced characters. Take James Cameron’s Aliens (1986), which develops Ellen Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) into a more complex protagonist who takes a more proactive role to protect a child. This shift leads to more action set-pieces, shifting the tone of the Alien franchise from a gnarly space horror to an action-filled blockbuster.

The Wachowskis drew direct inspiration from cyberpunk media to create The Matrix, which is now a seminal addition to the genre. While calling this first entry an action movie feels a bit reductive, the fight choreography in The Matrix is nothing short of revolutionary. The concept of “bullet time” was popularized by the film, where this multi-camera time-slice technique was incorporated into its stylized fight sequences.
points: Great action movies also have stakes that feel real.
They break genre conventions, use fights to flesh out characters, and balance out frenetic action with quieter moments.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it
articles.summary: A new report suggests that Xbox has capped its cloud gaming usage to 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers because that's when the service stops being profitable.
body: According to Windows Central, which cites unnamed Microsoft sources, that's not an arbitrary cap and is, allegedly, set at Microsoft's own break-even threshold as any usage beyond that costs the company money.

Windows Central ties the cost pressure to a wider squeeze on server memory caused by Microsoft's AI investments, with Azure capacity increasingly prioritised for AI workloads over game streaming. It frames the caps as part of a broader cost-cutting pattern across Xbox, alongside recent layoffs and cancelled projects, as the division comes under pressure to turn a bigger profit.

As Connor reported for us in the week, according to a 2025 report from Statista, US gamers spent an average of 9.5 hours per week playing video games, UK gamers 6.38 hours, and a worldwide average of 6.56 hours was recorded.
Despite Xbox scaling back its cloud gaming plans and the seemingly endless issues caused by the ramping up of AI data centres, industry giants remain bullish on cloud gaming.

articles.title: The 8 Biggest Manhunter Theories in 'Lanterns'
articles.summary: HBO’s Lanterns has proven to be one of the best new additions to James Gunn’s DC Universe. The series brings together Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and drops them into a decade-hopping murder mystery set in a small rural town where nothing seems right.
body: At the center of it all is a mysterious Manhunter. Not to be confused with the DC hero of the same name, the Manhunters are an army of artificial police created by the Guardians of the Universe long before the Green Lantern Corps. After going rogue, their mission of maintaining order violently devolved into a genocidal crusade. Lanterns shifts that history ever so slightly by turning the live-action Manhunters into synthetic shapeshifters capable of deep-cover infiltration, making the secret identity of the one hiding out in Rushville the core tension of the show.

Given Lanterns is a murder mystery wrapped in a superhero story, no one is above suspicion. Before the next episode airs, let’s take a look at some of the most compelling theories as to who might be the Manhunter, and what that might say about their ultimate goal in Lanterns.

articles.title: Saber CCO says the studio isn't changing up its comms strategy after recent controversies: 'There's always some dust up'
articles.summary: In a recent interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens at this year's Gamescom, Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits admitted the studio's leadership had a reputation for saying precisely what it means—"sometimes we 'say what we mean' too much," he laughed.
body: "I've been in the industry for so long, and there's always some dust up," Willits explained. "People got mad at Saber because we put World War Z on Epic, and people were like, 'oh, Saber's destroying the industry.' Now 30 million people have played World War Z. And the games will speak for themselves, even in our experiment with Rideshare [Stimulator]."

If you haven't been keeping up with the latest drama Saber Interactive has courted, here's the skinny: former Saber Interactive writer Stella Sacco claimed she was fired and replaced with AI during the development of Rideshare Stimulator.

Saber's comms department initially put out a fairly benign statement disputing the details of the claim, but CEO Matt Karch subsequently issued a statement to This Week In Videogames that was both aggressively pro-AI, and personally insulting to Sacco.
Karch apologized privately to Sacco before releasing a statement reflecting on the incident which itself contained a targeted barb for a different games industry writer that has since been edited.

articles.title: Sony clarifies PlayStation disc production is dropping by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent
articles.summary: Sony has pushed back on a wave of reports suggesting PlayStation disc manufacturing is about to be gutted by 90 percent after comments from a Sony DADC executive were allegedly misunderstood.
body: According to Game, which went directly to Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation (DADC) for clarity, output is actually expected to dip by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent.

"To clarify and avoid any misleading information: in that statement Dietmar anticipated an overall product volume decline by 10 percent, not a decline down to 10 percent," a Sony DADC spokesperson told Game, referring to comments made by DADC chief Dietmar Tanzer to an Austrian broadcaster in July.
The spokesperson didn't say what happens beyond 2028, and directed further questions on reorders to PlayStation's own PR team, which didn't respond to Game's queries.

The confusion stems from PlayStation's July announcement that it will stop producing physical discs for new games from January 2028 onward, though already-released titles and games still slated for disc release before that date aren't affected, and reorders will continue afterwards.

articles.title: Dwarf Fortress co-creator Tarn Adams was amazed other devs had heard of his game the first time he went to a convention: 'I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing'
articles.summary: Dwarf Fortress is a bit like caviar—not everyone's into it, but the people who are describe their experiences with it like a religious awakening. But the game's legendary co-creator, Tarn Adams, didn't even know it had a big following for many years, as he told PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens in a recent…
body: "It was something like 2013, 14 going to PAX in Seattle, and there was an indie mega booth at the time," he recalled. "Of the 50 or 60 games showing—I'm just ballparking the numbers—I'd say 90% of them heard of Dwarf Fortress and also had a very amazed fan-ish response when we were introduced." It was the first time Adams had a sense of the reach his game had.

"That was crazy. I had no idea that that was even a thing," he said. "I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing … I enjoyed it. I try to have good moral qualities, but I am apparently subject to all forms of flattery and vanity and such."

If he could go back in time, he wouldn't so as to not "disrupt the timeline." But if he could go back in time without the risk of doing that, Adams said might encourage himself to evangelize the game more in its early days.

"I'd probably be more confident about getting it in front of more people sooner. I didn't know the people to do that, though, so I'd probably be like 'go meet some more people,'" he said. "From the release of the game in 2006 up until around 2013, I didn't meet another game developer really, except maybe one or two at a Dwarf Fortress-specific meet."

articles.title: Go grandmaster becomes first human to win series against advanced AI engine in 3-hour match
articles.summary: As reported by The Korea Economic Daily, top-ranked Go grandmaster Shin Jin-seo became the first human to defeat the AI platform KataGo on July 21. It's a surprising, encouraging sign of human capabilities almost 30 years after supercomputer Deep Blue's historic defeat of Chess grandmaster Garry…
body: Go is believed to be the oldest board game that is still widely played, originating in China and beating out Chess by at least 1400 years, give or take. The strategy game sees players in control of different-colored stones, working to encircle their opponent's pieces, capturing territory and stones to achieve victory. Like Chess, its complexity, ubiquity, and the large amount of study and data surrounding the game made Go a fruitful tool for machine learning research.

Shin, 26, is the first human to win an official, three-game series against KataGo, which the Korea Economic Daily described as "the world's premier artificial intelligence Go engine." Shin's odds were long, especially considering that, 10 years ago, Go grandmaster Lee Sedol was decisively defeated by Google's AlphaGo engine⁠—the technology has only advanced in the intervening years.

articles.title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
articles.summary: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media.
body: While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.
People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

body: The complete Elden Ring package lands on Switch 2. Visually speaking we're getting a match for the last-gen PS4 release in core settings - though as a plus, Switch 2's frame-rate exceeds that older Sony release, while its resolution locks at the target 1080p more consistently. Comparisons against Series S are less flattering meanwhile. The lack of DLSS is also perhaps a missed opportunity, but on the whole Nintendo's handheld puts in a robust rendition of a true From Software classic.

videos.summary: SlashZero is a 3D side-scrolling action roguelike game.
body: As a player, you will become a time hacker and be able to traverse across multiple timelines.
Make full use of your action skills and combat strategies, collect items, hunt for clues, piece together the truth, and bring down the final boss!
The feel of the controls, the build configuration, and every aspect of the combat are entirely up to you!
